sentences.text: The known fossil of Scipionyx is a juvenile approximately 46.1 cm long, though the preserved length of the holotype is estimated at 23.7 cm.
The adult form and size of this dinosaur remain unknown.
It was a bipedal predator with a long tail that balanced its horizontal rump.
Scipionyx likely had primitive feathers, although no skin or feather remains have been found in the fossil.

Only one fossil of Scipionyx is known, discovered in 1981 by amateur paleontologist Giovanni Todesco in the Le Cavere quarry near Pietraroja, Italy. This find made it the first dinosaur discovered in Italy, and it was brought to scientific attention in 1993.
The specimen is famous for preserving large areas of petrified soft tissue, including muscles and intestines.

Half-digested remains of lizards and fish found in the fossil indicate Scipionyx ate these animals. The backward position of the prey bone cluster suggests Scipionyx had a dual stomach structure with a proventriculus and a muscular gizzard. A subsequent intestine part interpreted as the jejunum surfaces nearby and slightly above the duodenum, while faeces are still present in the final part of the rectum.

The genus Scipionyx and the species Scipionyx samniticus were described by dal Sasso and Signore in 1998. They assigned it to the Coelurosauria, a group of theropods. A 2011 cladistic analysis indicated Scipionyx was a basal member of the Compsognathidae and the sister species of Orkoraptor.
Scipionyx lived in Italy during the Early Cretaceous, approximately 113 million years ago. More specifically, it lived during the Albian stage, between 113.2 and 110.1 million years ago.

Scientists disagree on how Scipionyx breathed based on the position of its internal organs. A 2011 study reinterpreted a feature previously seen as a reduced hyposphene-hypantrum complex as a pair of tendon attachment points. In 1999, Philip J. Currie hypothesized that tubes found on the tail base represented protofeather filaments. Dal Sasso and Maganuco considered it likely that Scipionyx had protofeathers in life, citing their presence in related compsognathids.
